author: Daniel
content:
"我亲爱的！
One week ago we sat in an Uber on the way to the airport. 
We went to the gate, hand in hand. We stood embracing each other, physically encircling each other. 

I watched you stand in line, turn around and smile and wave at me. I saw you through a sea of people, a shining striped beacon whose light stands out from afar. 

The distance increased, I could no longer see you but I knew you were still close. You made me realize that distance is just a number. Whether you're in Paris or a couple hundred feet from me obscured by the airport walls, we keep one another with us in our hearts, wherever we go (+ Whatsapp helps a lot haha). 

I miss you, but all that separates us is distance. I yearn for the day I can hold you in my arms again, soon. 

Love, 
Daniel - Misser of Echo"
title: Misser of Echo

author: Daniel
content:
Echo! The time has arrived at last for us to reunite again. 
I have begun my journey, with a singular destination in mind. 
Travelling to see one's partner is truly something special, even beautifully poetic. 
My body locomoting towards my source of light and happiness, my mind focused 
on you, giddy with anticipation. 

When I consider whether I like coming to you, or you coming to me, I would say
I prefer coming to you, my home and harbor. I guess I am lucky this time! 

At the same time this reminds me of all the times you have travelled to be with me. 
Know that I am grateful for this, and everything you do, your smile, your voice, your entire existence. I am proud to call you my wife.

Lovingly yours, virtual and soon analog,
Daniel
title: Progressing pilgrim

author: Echo
content:
Bebe,

I am currently doing the CI lecture, and I felt a huge strike of hollowness. Fun fact, it's actually the same lecturer I encountered in Harvard, I probably had skipped his class to date you. Now we come again, skipped his class to write to you.

I just really lost all my interests in this domain. Feels like being hunted by this field for a couple of years, no idea why I still come back over and over for this kind of class.

Oxford is a bit boring, well, as boring as I remembered at least. Especially, right now, without you, no city has soul.  I don't get really driven to really make any connections in a city where I don't stay long, with all the people with whom we only talk about AI. I know that I am being very prejudiced, can't help.

I count the days until the next time I will see you, and keep remembering the memories we had together. That's the light of the North Star in my life now. 

I really miss you a lot, a lot, more than I can bear. 


Echo
